pois.name: Kraton Yogyakarta
pois.description: The royal palace of the Sultan of Yogyakarta, built in 1755 by Sultan Hamengkubuwono I. A living palace — the current Sultan and his family still reside here. The complex of Javanese pavilions, courts, and gardens is the finest example of traditional Javanese palace architecture.

pois.name: Taman Sari Water Castle
pois.description: A 18th-century royal pleasure garden and bathing complex, originally surrounded by a man-made lake. The subterranean mosque, bathing pools, and ornamental towers make this one of Java's most atmospheric heritage sites.

pois.name: Alun-Alun Kidul
pois.description: The South Royal Square — home to the famous 'Masangin' ritual where visitors attempt to walk blindfolded between two sacred banyan trees. The square is packed nightly with families, street food carts, and lit-up bicycle taxis.

pois.name: Museum Sonobudoyo
pois.description: Yogyakarta's principal museum of Javanese culture, in a beautiful traditional Javanese building facing the North Square. Houses one of Java's finest collections of batik, kris daggers, masks, and Hindu-Buddhist bronzes.

pois.name: Kampung Wisata Taman Sari
pois.description: The village immediately surrounding Taman Sari — a maze of narrow lanes filled with batik workshops, silver shops, and wayang puppet studios. One of Yogyakarta's most authentic craft neighbourhoods.
